name: RSI(2) pullback in uptrend on an index ETF (Connors)
rule: Daily bars, one index ETF. If Close > SMA(200) and RSI(2) < entry_level, buy at the close (or next open). Sell at the close when Close > SMA(5); alternatives: RSI(2) > 70, or Close > previous day's High. No price stop; optional time stop after max_hold_days. One position, full allocation.
instruments: Liquid NSE index ETFs (NIFTYBEES, BANKBEES, JUNIORBEES), delivery; index futures only with much larger capital
reported_performance: SPY 1993-c.2025 (QuantifiedStrategies): buy RSI2<10, sell RSI2>80: 0.9% per trade, ~9% a year, max DD 34%, 28% exposure; with SMA200 filter 0.95% per trade, CAGR 6.8%, DD 31%; exit close>yesterday's high: 0.5% per trade, 76% wins, DD 15%. S&P 500 index 1957-2023 (Alvarez): low RSI2 followed by above-average returns only since 1995.
feasibility_reason: ETF delivery round trip about 0.07-0.17% at Rs 50k-1.5L (sell STT 0.001%, to confirm on contract note) versus 0.5-0.95% reported gross per trade; 5-15 trades a year; one position; daily data only. Edge on NSE ETFs untested.

name: RSI(2) oversold stock portfolio with position cap
rule: Universe: point-in-time large-cap/F&O stocks with Close > SMA(200) and index > SMA(200). Signal at close: RSI(2) < entry_level and Close < SMA(5). Rank signals by 100-day historical volatility, highest first; skip stocks with a gap down >= 5% in the last 10 days. Buy next open, equal weight, at most max_positions. Sell next open after Close > SMA(5), or after max_hold_days.
instruments: Nifty 100/200 or F&O-list stocks, delivery
reported_performance: S&P 500 constituents 1996-Nov 2025 (Concretum): 114,189 trades, mean 0.45% per trade, 64% hit rate, but no capped random subsample of 5 trades a day matched that mean. S&P 500 2004-2024, 10 slots (Quantitativo): ~17% a year, Sharpe ~0.87, max DD 34%, +0.36% per trade. Russell 3000 2000-2022 (Alvarez): edge shrinking; negative in 2020 and 2022.
feasibility_reason: Angel One delivery round trip is 0.46% at Rs 30k (5 slots) and 0.62% at Rs 15k (10 slots) before spread, about equal to the US gross edge per trade; signals cluster in sell-offs so 5 slots miss the best trades; no overnight shorts.

name: Oversold setup with next-day limit entry below the close (Alvarez)
rule: Setup at close: liquid stock, Close > SMA(100), RSI(2) < setup_level. Next day place a day-only limit buy limit_pct below the setup close, only for as many names as free slots, ranked by 100-day historical volatility, highest first. Exit at next open after RSI(2) > exit_level or after max_hold_days. No stop.
instruments: Nifty 100/200 or F&O-list stocks, delivery
reported_performance: Russell 3000, 2007-Jun 2021 (Alvarez): versus next-open entry, limit entry raised CAR 21%, cut exposure 33% and doubled average profit per trade (relative figures only). 2007-Jun 2018 base version 'really disappointing', low-teens CAR at best, weak 2016-2017.
feasibility_reason: Fewer fills lowers cost and unfilled orders are free at Angel One, but each filled delivery round trip still costs 0.46-0.62% at Rs 15-30k; fills are adversely selected; untested in India.

name: Connors R3 (three falling RSI(2) days)
rule: Daily bars, ETF. Conditions: Close > SMA(200); RSI(2) has fallen three days in a row and the first fall started from below 60; RSI(2) today < 10. Buy at today's close. Sell at the close when RSI(2) > 70. No stop.
instruments: Liquid NSE index and sector ETFs, delivery
reported_performance: QuantifiedStrategies, ETF inception to Dec 2020, no costs: SPY 1.28% per trade (Connors to 2008: 1.16%), QQQ 1.04% (1.24%), EEM 0.45% (0.91%), EWH 0.31% (1.18%), XLF 0.26% (0.46%); fewer fills than Connors; several ETFs lost half their edge after publication.
feasibility_reason: ETF round trip 0.07-0.17%; a handful of trades a year; too infrequent to stand alone and unverified on NSE ETFs.

name: Connors %b (three closes with %b below 0.2)
rule: Daily bars, ETF. %b = (Close - LowerBB) / (UpperBB - LowerBB) with Bollinger(bb_length, bb_width). If Close > SMA(200) and %b < 0.2 on each of the last three days, buy at the close. Sell at the close when %b > 0.8. No stop.
instruments: Liquid NSE index and sector ETFs, delivery
reported_performance: QuantifiedStrategies, 20 US ETFs since inception: 677 trades, 75% wins, 0.76% per trade, profit factor 1.9, CAGR 4.84%, max DD 16%, 17% exposure; 10-day lookback CAGR 8.2%. Connors' band settings could not be replicated.
feasibility_reason: ETF costs small against 0.76% gross per trade; low exposure; band parameters uncertain so a grid must be tested.

name: Connors 3-day high/low method
rule: Daily bars, ETF. Conditions: Close > SMA(200); Close < SMA(5); each of the last three days had a lower High and a lower Low than the day before. Buy at today's close. Sell at the close when Close > SMA(5). No stop.
instruments: Liquid NSE index and sector ETFs, delivery
reported_performance: QuantifiedStrategies, 20 US ETFs, 2000-Nov 2020: 1,616 trades, 0.38% per trade, CAGR 5.74%, profit factor 1.53, max DD 16.4%; 13 of 20 ETFs did worse than in Connors' pre-2009 test.
feasibility_reason: ETF round trip 0.07-0.17% versus 0.38% gross per trade leaves a thin margin; simple daily rules; edge decayed after publication.

name: N-day down streak / Connors multiple days down
rule: Daily bars, ETF or liquid stock. If Close > SMA(200), Close < SMA(5) and at least down_days of the last window_days closes were lower than the prior close (variant: streak_days consecutive lower closes), buy at the close. Sell at the close when Close > SMA(5). No stop.
instruments: Liquid NSE index and sector ETFs, delivery
reported_performance: No opened source gives numbers (QuantifiedStrategies re-test paywalled). Alvarez lists 3-5 consecutive down days as a working pullback measure. Nifty since 1994 (Capitalmind 2011): after 6 straight up closes the next-day expectancy was +0.13% (61 cases), i.e. up streaks continued rather than reversed; no Indian down-streak test found.
feasibility_reason: Operationally trivial in ETFs with low cost; evidence is weak and the only Indian streak evidence points to continuation.

name: Double Seven / N-day-low dip buying
rule: Daily bars, index ETF. If Close > SMA(200) and today's Close is the lowest close of the last lookback days, buy at the close. Exit A (Double Seven): sell at the close when Close is the highest close of the last lookback days. Exit B: sell at the first close above the previous close. No stop.
instruments: Liquid NSE index ETFs, delivery
reported_performance: SPY since 1993 (QuantifiedStrategies): Double Seven 154 trades, 1.18% per trade, 82.5% wins, CAGR 6.3%, max DD 33%, 26% exposure; multi-ETF 1,189 trades, 0.63% per trade, 'almost all gains happened before 2010'. Exit B: 329 trades, 0.52% per trade, 76% wins, CAGR 5.7% vs 9.5% buy and hold.
feasibility_reason: Few trades and small ETF costs; average losers exceed average winners and capital idles about 75% of the time.

name: Internal bar strength (IBS) on an index ETF
rule: Daily bars, one index ETF. IBS = (Close - Low) / (High - Low). Buy at the close when IBS < buy_level. Sell at the close of the first later day with IBS > sell_level. No stop. Must be filled at or just before the close.
instruments: Liquid NSE index ETFs (NIFTYBEES, BANKBEES, JUNIORBEES), delivery
reported_performance: SPY 1993-c.2025, no costs (QuantifiedStrategies): 919 trades, 0.41% per trade, 68% wins, CAGR 12.5% vs 9.9%, max DD 26%; next-open entry cuts it to 0.31%. US-listed equity ETFs to May 2013 (Pagonidis): +0.35% next day after IBS<0.2, -0.13% after IBS>0.8; little or no effect in locally listed ETFs of seven other markets. No usable evidence on NSE-listed instruments: only US-listed India ETFs (EPI +0.39%/-0.30%) and a Marketcalls Nifty futures test (2007-2014) whose results could not be read.
feasibility_reason: About 30 ETF round trips a year at 0.07-0.17% each (2-5% a year) versus 0.3-0.4% gross per trade in the US; one position; depends on executing at the NSE close and on the effect existing locally, which is unproven.

name: RSI(3) pullback with IBS filter (Pagonidis)
rule: Daily bars, index ETF. Cutler RSI(3) uses simple averages of up and down closes. Base state turns on at a close with RSI(3) < 10 and stays on while RSI(3) <= 40. Hold the ETF overnight only on days when the base state is on and IBS <= 0.5; otherwise flat. Orders at the close. No stop.
instruments: Liquid NSE index ETFs, delivery
reported_performance: US-listed equity ETFs to May 2013 (Pagonidis): the IBS filter removed about 43% of days in the market and raised total return by 9.6% on average. QuantifiedStrategies 'IBS + second indicator': SPY 278 trades, 0.8% per trade, 78% wins, max DD 23.75%; QQQ 232 trades, 1.33% per trade.
feasibility_reason: ETF implementation, daily data, low cost per trade; more round trips than plain RSI because the IBS filter toggles the position; untested on NSE.

name: Lowest-IBS rotation across an ETF basket
rule: Each day at the close compute IBS for every ETF in the basket. Buy the n_long ETFs with the lowest IBS (optionally only if IBS < max_ibs); hold until the next close, then repeat. Academic version also shorts the highest-IBS ETF. Close-to-close execution only.
instruments: Basket of liquid NSE equity ETFs (broad, bank, next-50, sector), delivery, long-only
reported_performance: 15 US-listed country ETFs, 2009-2019, no commissions (Pandey and Joshi): long-short Sharpe 2.9, best baskets 3.7-3.9, long-only leg 1.3-2.0; open-to-open execution gives Sharpe about -0.3 to 0.4.
feasibility_reason: About 250 round trips a year: roughly 17% of capital a year in charges at Rs 1.5L per trade and more if split; few liquid Indian ETFs; effect documented only for US-listed ETFs at the US close.

name: Bollinger lower-band reversion
rule: Daily bars. Buy at the close when Close < SMA(bb_length) - bb_width * StdDev(bb_length). Sell at the close when Close > SMA(bb_length). Optional filter Close > SMA(200). No stop in the tested version.
instruments: Index ETFs; liquid stocks
reported_performance: S&P 500 since 1993 (QuantifiedStrategies): trailed buy and hold by a wide margin and 'since 2018 it has been a losing strategy'. Indian and Taiwanese academic tests seen only as search snippets (unverified).
feasibility_reason: Executable cheaply in ETFs, but this is the weakest-evidenced rule in the family and has been negative since 2018 in the US; for stocks delivery costs exceed any documented edge.

name: Stretch below short moving average / ATR band
rule: Daily bars. If Close > SMA(200) and Close <= SMA(ma_length) * (1 - stretch_pct/100), buy at the close. ATR variant: Close < SMA(ma_length) - atr_mult * ATR(atr_length). Sell at the close when Close > SMA(ma_length). Time stop max_hold_days.
instruments: Index ETFs; liquid stocks
reported_performance: QuantifiedStrategies 'rubber band' (Keltner/ATR band, exact settings members-only), SPY: 328 trades, 0.45% per trade, CAGR 6.1%, 20% exposure, profit factor 2, max DD 16%. Alvarez gives the percentage-stretch parameter ranges without statistics.
feasibility_reason: ETF version has low cost against 0.45% gross per trade; ATR multiplier and length are assumptions because the source rules are paywalled.

name: Williams %R oversold with strength exit
rule: Daily bars, index ETF. %R(n) = -100 * (HighestHigh_n - Close) / (HighestHigh_n - LowestLow_n). Buy at the close when %R < -90. Sell at the close when Close > previous day's High or %R > -30. No stop.
instruments: Liquid NSE index ETFs, delivery
reported_performance: SPY since 1993 (QuantifiedStrategies): CAGR 11.9% vs 10.3% buy and hold, 22% exposure, 598 trades, 0.6% per trade, max DD 17%, profit factor 2.2; all lookbacks 2-24 had profit factor >= 2.
feasibility_reason: About 18 ETF trades a year at 0.07-0.17% each; nearly the same information as IBS/RSI(2), so not an independent strategy.

name: ConnorsRSI pullback
rule: Daily bars. CRSI = (RSI(3) + RSI(streak, 2) + PercentRank(1-day return, 100)) / 3, streak = signed run of up/down closes. If Close > SMA(200) and CRSI < entry_level, buy at the close. Sell at the close when Close > previous day's High or CRSI > exit_level. No stop.
instruments: Index ETFs; liquid stocks
reported_performance: S&P 500 since 1993 (QuantifiedStrategies), 2-day lookbacks, buy <10, exit close > yesterday's high: 293 trades, 0.5% per trade, 75% wins, 'a few big losing periods'; plain RSI(2) with the same rules did better (385 trades, 0.66%).
feasibility_reason: Feasible in ETFs at low cost, but the one opened test shows no advantage over RSI(2); low priority.

name: DV2 (Varadi oscillator) oversold stock portfolio
rule: DV2 = 100 * percent rank over rank_lookback days of SMA2(Close / ((High+Low)/2)). Universe: index members with Close > SMA(200) and 6-month return > 0. If yesterday's DV2 < 10, buy at the open; if signals exceed free slots take highest ATR(14)/Close first; at most max_positions equal slots. Sell at the next open after Close > previous day's High.
instruments: Nifty 100/200 or F&O-list stocks, delivery
reported_performance: S&P 500 point-in-time, 2004-2024 (Quantitativo): 17.4% a year, Sharpe 0.87, max DD 34%, ~475 trades a year, 64.8% wins, +0.36% per trade; with 6-month filter 20.9% a year, Sharpe 1.01. Returns fall as assumed costs rise.
feasibility_reason: At 10 slots, ~475 trades a year cost about Rs 44,000 (29% of capital) at Angel One, more than the reported gross return; only a low-frequency 3-5 slot version is worth testing. Percent-rank lookback not confirmed.

name: Turnaround Tuesday (buy weak Monday close)
rule: Daily bars, index ETF. If today is Monday, Close < Friday's Close and IBS < 0.5, buy at the close. Sell at the close when Close > previous day's High, or 4 trading days after entry. Strict one-day variant: Monday Close <= 0.99 * Friday Close, sell Tuesday's close.
instruments: Liquid NSE index ETFs, delivery; stock-basket variant possible
reported_performance: SPY from 1993 with 0.03% costs (QuantifiedStrategies): strict variant 212 trades, 0.3% per trade, CAGR 1.8%, 56% wins; IBS<0.5 with 4-day exit 495 trades, 0.46% per trade, CAGR 7%, 17% exposure, 69% wins. Stock version (StrategyQuant, 20 years, 0.1% commission): Nasdaq 100 CAGR ~10%, S&P 500 ~15%. Disputed by Price Action Lab (paywalled).
feasibility_reason: ETF version makes 7-17 trades a year at negligible cost; the weekday effect is untested on NSE and the plain version's edge is small.

name: Weekly loser rotation (Lehmann; de Groot et al.)
rule: Each weekend: universe = largest universe_size stocks, stock Close > SMA(200) and index Close > SMA(200). Rank by rank_days closing range (Close - LowestLow) / (HighestHigh - LowestLow), lowest first (academic: prior-week return). Buy the n_long lowest at Monday's open, equal weight; sell after one week; repeat. Academic version also shorts the highest.
instruments: Nifty 100 stocks, delivery, long leg only
reported_performance: US 1990-2009 net of institutional costs (de Groot et al. via Quantpedia): -31.4 bp a week for 1,500 stocks, +10.6 bp for 500, +29.0 bp for the 100 largest (long-short). Long-only top-5 on S&P 500, 2007-Oct 2017 (Alvarez): RSI and return rankings no better than random; best closing-range CAR 8.26%, 0.28% per trade. India, NSE 500 2014-2021: weekly horizons showed momentum, not reversal.
feasibility_reason: Five positions turned weekly is ~260 delivery round trips, about Rs 36,000 (24% of capital) a year; the long-only version failed a random-ranking test and Indian weekly data favour momentum.

name: One-month reversal with turnover filter (Jegadeesh; Medhat-Schmeling)
rule: At month-end rank a large-cap universe by 1-month return. Exclude stocks in the top turnover_exclude_pct of 1-month turnover (volume / shares outstanding). Buy the n_long worst performers at the next open, equal weight; hold one month; rebalance. Academic version also shorts the best performers.
instruments: Nifty 100/200 stocks, delivery, long leg only
reported_performance: US 1934-1987 about 2% a month (Jegadeesh, cited by Da et al.). US 1968-2010: 0.81% raw a month equal-weighted, zero among large stocks (Hameed-Mian). US 1963-2018: 0.84% a month in large caps but average cost 1.94% a month exceeds gross; reversal only in low-turnover stocks, momentum in the top turnover decile; faded after 2011 (Medhat-Schmeling). India: reversal reported mainly in illiquid stocks (unverified snippet).
feasibility_reason: Only 60-120 delivery round trips a year (5.5-7.5% of capital), but the long-only large-cap edge is roughly zero in US data and Indian liquid stocks show one-month momentum when turnover is high.

name: Industry-relative one-month reversal (Hameed-Mian)
rule: At month-end compute each stock's 1-month return minus the equal-weighted 1-month return of its industry. Buy the n_long stocks with the most negative difference, at most max_per_industry per industry, equal weight, next open; hold one month; rebalance. Academic version weights by minus the difference and shorts outperformers.
instruments: Nifty 100/200 stocks with a sector map, delivery, long leg only
reported_performance: US 1968-2010 (Hameed-Mian): 1.14% raw / 0.97% risk-adjusted a month versus 0.63% for market-relative reversal; 0.94% in 2000-2010; 0.53% value-weighted; 0.47% among large stocks; above 1% a month after market declines. Residual reversal (Blitz et al.): profitable net of costs in large caps after 1990.
feasibility_reason: Low turnover (60 round trips a year, about 5.5% of capital) and the best-supported large-cap reversal signal, but evidence is US long-short; the long-only Indian version is untested and needs a sector classification.

name: Daily cross-sectional contrarian, open to close
rule: Each morning rank a liquid universe by cumulative return over the last formation_days closes. At the open short the n_per_side best performers and buy the n_per_side worst, equal rupee size, intraday product; close all at the close. Lo-MacKinlay variant: weights proportional to minus (stock return - market return) for the prior day.
instruments: F&O-list / Nifty 200 stocks, intraday (MIS) both sides
reported_performance: NSE 500, 2014-2021, no costs (arXiv 2302.13245): best loser-minus-winner 6.04% a month, max DD -13.7%; profit came from the short-winner leg, both legs negative open-to-close. US gross: 1.38% a day in 1995 falling to 0.13% in 2007 (Khandani-Lo); 0.30% a day on trade prices but 0.18% on quote midpoints, 1998-2010 (Nagel).
feasibility_reason: Delivery is impossible (0.3-0.6% a day). Intraday costs are 0.07-0.19% per name per day plus open-auction slippage against a gross 0.2-0.4% a day; needs intraday shorting, leverage and daily automation; long-only version lost money in the Indian study.

name: Buy large, liquid Indian stocks after a large one-month fall
rule: At month-end, among large liquid NSE stocks, flag any stock whose 1-month return <= -drop_pct. Buy at the next open, equal slots, at most max_positions; hold hold_months, then sell. No stop in the source; a max_loss_pct time-independent exit is an optional addition.
instruments: Nifty 100/200 stocks, delivery
reported_performance: Large liquid Indian stocks (Parthasarathy and Sendilvelu, Economic Thought Journal 2022): significant reversals after large monthly declines and rises for up to six months, stronger after larger shocks, robust to microstructure and market effects; magnitudes not available in the abstract. Threshold is an assumption.
feasibility_reason: A handful of delivery trades a year held for months, so 0.3-0.5% cost is minor; main risks are value traps (ideally screen out fraud or results-driven falls, which needs event data) and no stop; effect sizes unknown.

name: Opening gap-down fade on the index
rule: Intraday. If the open is between min_gap_pct and max_gap_pct below yesterday's close and yesterday's IBS < 0.25, buy at the open. Target = entry price + target_fraction * gap size; if not reached, exit at the close. No stop. Skip gaps beyond max_gap_pct.
instruments: Index ETF intraday (MIS) or index futures
reported_performance: SPY Jan 2010-Aug 2012 (QuantifiedStrategies): 110 fills, 98 winners, 0.19% per fill on end-of-day data; 89 fills, 0.22% (long) and 0.08% (short) on 30-minute data; author calls the first result 'probably too good to be true'. No verified Nifty fill-rate data exists; Nifty opening returns show momentum (JGU summary).
feasibility_reason: Intraday ETF round trip 0.07-0.13% takes half or more of a 0.1-0.2% edge; one Nifty futures lot uses the whole account; needs intraday data and open-auction execution.

name: Take index reversal entries only when implied volatility is elevated
rule: Overlay on an index-ETF reversal entry (default IBS < 0.2 at the close, exit IBS > 0.8). Take the entry only if India VIX close > SMA(India VIX, vix_sma). Otherwise stay flat. Exits unchanged. Test the opposite filter (VIX below a cap) for multi-day stock pullback systems.
instruments: Liquid NSE index ETFs, delivery; India VIX as input
reported_performance: SPY IBS system (QuantifiedStrategies): VIX > 100-day average raises average trade from 0.41% to 0.53% and profit factor from 1.92 to 2.19, but is sensitive to the average length. US 1998-2010 (Nagel): reversal returns strongly predicted by VIX. Contrary: RSI(2) stock systems lost in 2020 and 2022 (Alvarez).
feasibility_reason: An overlay that reduces trade count; needs India VIX daily history; sign of the effect differs between index one-day reversal and stock pullback systems.

name: Pre-earnings loser reversal (So and Wang)
rule: For large-cap stocks with earnings date t: compute average return over days t-4 to t-2. Buy the bottom quintile at the close of t-2 and hold through the close of t+1. Academic version also shorts the top quintile. Equal weights.
instruments: Large-cap stocks with a reliable results calendar, delivery
reported_performance: US 1996-2011, largest size quintile (Quantpedia): indicative 6.5% a year long-short, volatility 3.76%; reversals six times larger around earnings than otherwise.
feasibility_reason: Roughly 0.16% gross per 3-day window for the long-short spread versus 0.27-0.62% delivery cost per round trip; holds single stocks through results; needs event data.

name: RSI crosses back above 30, exit above 70 (Indian index stocks)
rule: Daily bars, long-only. Buy at the next open after RSI(rsi_length) crosses above 30 from below. Sell at the next open after RSI crosses above 70. Equal slots, at most max_positions; skip signals when full. No stop in the source.
instruments: Nifty 50 / Next 50 / Nifty 500 stocks, delivery
holding_period: Weeks to months (about one trade per stock per year)
reported_performance: 25-year backtest on Indian index stocks (Share.Market/PhonePe, 2025): with 21-period RSI, 79.05% win rate and 15.65% average return per trade; long-only worked, short-only and long-short lost. No costs; current constituents used throughout (survivorship bias).
feasibility_reason: Very low turnover so delivery costs of 0.3-0.6% per trade are minor; capital is tied up for months and reported returns are inflated by survivorship bias.
